result.summary: Adds a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow that runs weekly to verify the validity and expiration date of the Windows code signing certificate. If the certificate is within 90 days of expiry or has already expired, the job opens an issue in the repository with certificate details and the checked commit. Duplicate issues are prevented by searching for existing open or closed issues matching the expiry title.
result.problem: There is no automated monitoring for code signing certificate expiration, forcing maintainers to rely on release candidate cycles to discover expired certificates. If a minor or bugfix release must be published on short notice, discovering an expired certificate at that moment can delay the release.
evidence: PR description: 'Currently we have no automation in place to check that our code signing certificates are not expired or close to expiry. We have previously "relied on Release Candidates" as a dry-run for codesigners to realise that a certificate has expired and have time to fix it.'
result.changed_since_previous: The core approach remains unchanged from the previous version.
result.card: Adds a weekly GitHub Actions workflow to check the Windows code signing certificate and open an issue if it expires within 90 days. Bitcoin Core currently has no automated monitoring for certificate expiration, relying on release candidate cycles for codesigners to discover expired certificates. The author notes that relying on regular release cycles is prone to delaying urgent, short-notice bugfix releases. Duplicate issues are suppressed by checking for existing open or closed expiry reports.

risk.why: A bug in the workflow could fail to alert developers to certificate expiration or create duplicate GitHub issues.
